mainMissionDesc: Fragments of an unknown technology are scattered across the sector. Some stations guard them. Some NPCs know where they are. Finding all 4 fragments is the ultimate goal of a run.

lines: The sector awaits you.
Start by exploring the station and looking for work.
You're a Drifter. Congratulations — that's the polite term.
500 credits. 3 units of fuel. No particular skills.
The sector has seen thousands of people like you pass through.
Most didn't stay long.
But you'll surely make it. No. Probably not.
Try anyway.
vagabond.objective: Objective: survive long enough to have a story to tell.

lines: Your ship holds together with glue, wire, and your excessive optimism.
30% chance you lose your cargo on every trip.
You still decided to trade in space.
That's brave. It's also deeply irrational.
We'd like to wish you good luck.
We're going to do it anyway.
ferrailleur.objective: Objective: generate enough profit to offset your losses in transit.

lines: You owe someone money. A lot of money.
50 credits a day. Every day. No exceptions.
You don't really know who to. It's the kind of debt you'd rather not trace.
The good news: you start with 1,200 credits.
The bad news: you get it.
Run.
endette.objective: Objective: earn faster than you lose. This isn't a metaphor.

lines: Every trip costs you 100 credits more than everyone else.
We won't ask why. Not our business.
What we know: you have off-the-charts stamina and unpredictable reflexes.
And needs. Regular. Costly.
It can work. If the credits come in fast enough.
It can also end very badly. The margin is thin.
accro.objective: Objective: maintain the flow of credits to fund the road — and the rest.

lines: The universe doesn't like you.
That's not a figure of speech — it's a mechanical reality of your existence.
One good thing out of two will backfire on you.
Other pilots have luck or skill.
You have... perseverance? We suppose.
Good luck. No, seriously this time.
maudit.objective: Objective: find a path that doesn't involve too many good things.

lines: The sector runs on a simple rule: buy low, sell high.
Faction wars make prices fluctuate. So do world events.
You start at Port Meridian — a stable trade hub.
Explore the local market. Look for work. Identify profitable routes.
The first runs are for understanding the flows. After that, you optimize.
marchand.objective: Objective: reach 10,000 credits. Then aim for 100,000. Then the stars.

lines: You know engines better than you know yourself.
Your ship has superior fuel capacity — that opens routes others can't reach.
Start by exploring. Understanding the sector's geography is your edge.
Distant stations pay better. Deep zones reward endurance.
Your ship is your tool. Maintain it.
mecanicien.objective: Objective: map the sector and profit from it. You're built for long-range exploration.

lines: Space holds no more secrets for you — or almost none.
Neutral zones reward you better than others. Explore often.
Every station has a story. Some hold fragments of something bigger.
Narrative arcs trigger based on what you do and where you go.
Follow the threads. The sector has a memory.
explorateur.objective: Objective: see what the sector hides from those who don't dare look.

lines: You heal in clinics that don't officially exist.
Medicine earns you 50% more than others — that's your trade.
You can also heal yourself more effectively in combat.
Start at Port Meridian. Build up stock. Find routes with high medical demand.
Conflict zones pay the best. That's an uncomfortable reality.
medecin.objective: Objective: build a distribution network in a sector that needs it.

lines: You buy 20% cheaper than everyone else. That's a considerable edge.
In exchange: pirates know you. They show up twice as often.
You start at the Bas-Fonds de Vega — where good deals and bad encounters coexist.
Watch your route. Some corridors are more watched than others.
And if you get caught, you already know what to do.
contrebandier.objective: Objective: exploit your price edge before your enemies exploit you.

lines: Thirty years of wars. You survived things that killed better people than you.
You hit harder. You take less. You start with momentum.
The Citadelle Écarlate is your base — a place that suits you.
Combat quests pay you more. Station bosses are your specialty.
The sector needs people like you. Or fears them. Same thing.
veteran.objective: Objective: clean up the sector, faction by faction, boss by boss.

lines: You don't know how to fight. You don't need to.
300 credits arrive every 5 days, automatically. Your inheritance works for you.
The catch: you can't buy weapons. It's not in your upbringing.
Start at the Citadelle Écarlate. Build your trade network.
Money opens doors that force can't force open.
heritier.objective: Objective: become the sector's economic pillar without ever touching a weapon.

lines: You see station prices before you arrive. That's information others pay dearly for.
In combat you can hack enemy equipment. Systems hold no secrets for you.
Physically, you're vulnerable. Compensate with preparation.
Start at the Citadelle Écarlate. Identify the sector's information flows.
Everything is connected. You're the only one who can read the connections.
hackeur.objective: Objective: exploit information the way others exploit brute force.

lines: Pirates avoid you. That's not luck — it's your reputation.
You hit 50% harder. You start combat with momentum.
Peaceful stations don't want you. Not your problem.
You start at Fort Kharos — a place that understands what you are.
The sector has targets. Some carry bounties. Go get them.
seigneurDeGuerre.objective: Objective: impose your dominance over the sector, one boss at a time.
